title: Want to Sound More Confident? Raise Your Eyebrows!
paragraphs: You might think that sounding confident is all about choosing the right words and speaking clearly. But your facial expressions may matter more than you think!
A new study from the University of Glasgow suggests that something as simple as raising your eyebrows or briefly closing your eyes could make others think you're more sure of what you're saying.
The study involved 44 people: 22 native English speakers from Britain and 22 native Mandarin speakers from China.

The participants watched short videos of computer-generated faces answering "Yes" or "No" to questions such as, "Would they make a good leader?" or, "Will they finish the essay tonight?" The researchers changed how the faces moved their eyes and eyebrows while keeping the words and tone of voice the same.
Each participant watched 1,800 videos, judging how confident the speaker appeared, from "very doubtful" to "very confident."

The results were very similar for both the English-speaking group and the Mandarin-speaking group. Brief eye closure and raised brows made speakers seem more certain, while lowered brows and squinting had the opposite effect.
Also, the more the speaker lowered their eyebrows or squinted, the more doubtful they appeared. However, raising the eyebrows higher did not make the speaker seem any more confident.
"When interpreting speech, listeners draw on more than just the words and voice," said Jonas Nölle, who led the study.
While previous research has shown that gestures and tone of voice affect how we interpret speech, much less is known about the role facial expressions play in showing confidence.
The researchers say their findings show that facial expressions do more than just accompany speech — they help shape how we understand what others are saying.
So the next time you want to sound convincing, remember that your face may be speaking just as loudly as your words!
